regenerable_on: a guest carrying OpenZFS >= 2.3 for `zpool status -j`, with eight spare block devices: five for the raidz1, one hot spare, one log, one cache
note:
The first capture this product has ever taken of a pool with a spare in it, and the shape that found four layers of the same blindness at once.

A five-wide raidz1 on real virtio block devices with by-id aliases, plus a hot spare, a log device and a cache device. One member was then made to DISAPPEAR — the virtio driver unbound inside the guest, so the block device genuinely stopped existing rather than being softly offlined — and ZFS pulled the spare in by itself. What the payload holds is therefore the whole failure story in one document: a REMOVED leaf, the spare-3 pseudo-vdev the replacement creates inside the raidz group, the spare ONLINE at depth 3 doing the work and INUSE at pool level being accounted for, a resilver that has overwritten the scrub record, and a pool DEGRADED with Errors 0 because parity and the spare between them lost nothing.

Why no capture held this before: `zpool status -j` carries spares, logs and l2cache as TOP-LEVEL keys on the pool object rather than inside its vdevs tree, and every layer of this repository read only the tree. The adapter emitted no rows for them. The two mutation operators claiming to cover the class minted them nested, a shape zpool does not produce. The closure guard's extractor walked the tree too, so a real payload reported no group members present at all. And the scrub manifest classified only the tree, so the scrubber REFUSED to classify a payload holding a group vdev — which is why this capture could not have been taken until the manifest was extended. Each layer hid the next; the pair is committed so that none of them can go back.

Stated bound: the members are virtio disks, so `path` is a by-id alias and every leaf resolves to a kernel name. A pool on plain /dev/sdX with no alias tree resolves differently and is covered by corpus/storage/healthy, whose five unobservable Device records are the other half of that question.
anchors_note:
Read off payloads/status.json by hand, before any stream was generated.

State DEGRADED and Errors 0 are the pair that must not be conflated: the pool lost a device and lost no data, because raidz1 parity plus the spare covered it. Redundancy raidz1 tolerating 1 is anchored because the spare-3 pseudo-vdev sits at depth 2 inside the raidz group and a redundancy walk that counted members there — the shape the queue's open item is about — would grade this pool differently. ScanFunction RESILVER with LastScrubEndTime asserted ABSENT from the facts is the incident this product carries a fact pair for: ZFS keeps one scan record, the resilver overwrote the scrub's, and the time since the last real scrub is a value that exists and cannot be read, so it belongs on the unobservable channel and NOT among the facts. UnhealthyVdevs holds exactly three: the raidz group, the pseudo-vdev, and the leaf that vanished. It does NOT hold the spare — the spare is INUSE, which is to say it is doing its job, and a collector that listed it here would be raising an alarm about the device doing the saving. That omission is the anchor's whole point; it was the shipping behaviour until this capture was taken.
